text:
sre-oncall: :rotating_light: Heads up — EU3 GPU fleet is degrading fast. Over last 6m ~38% of gpu hosts in az-eu3-2 reporting kernel panics and OOM watchdog restarts. Autoscaler is flapping because kubelets are failing image pulls on restart. We currently have ~25% traffic already routed to fallback regions but latency-sensitive routes still prefer eu3. Proposing emergency measures for next 30m: apply per-customer soft caps for top noisy tenants, a conservative global token-rate-limit, and pause the heavy batch job queue 'embeddings-batch'. Need quick triage + visibility + customer comms plan.

sre-oncall: quick metrics: \n```\nhosts_total: 120\nhosts_healthy: 74\navg_p95_latency_eu3: 210ms (up from 95ms)\nimage_pull_fail_rate: 12%\nerror_budget_burn: 4.2%/min\n```\n
irene: Ack. Can we target only the heavy hitters? If we blanket soft cap we'll unnecessarily hurt small customers (esp trial orgs). Suggest top-10 by qps + any tenants with >100k tokens/min.

marcus: I can apply per-tenant softcaps. Send me the list and I’ll push a conservative cap (60% of usual). Also recommend pausing scheduled embeddings batches: `kubectl scale --replicas=0 deployment/embeddings-batch -n jobs` until healthy.

sre-oncall: thanks. Sending list now. Top noisy tenants (by recent qps): redwood-marketing, beta-retail-1, ai-saas-ops, partner-x, analytics-labs, bigsearch, corp-data, psi-ai, sparknotes, thirdparty-inc.

maria-se: For product/ops — should we trigger a short customer notice for the top affected tenants? We should avoid surprise for paying customers. Recommend an automated email + workspace PM for the top 5.

product-ops: +1. We can push a brief note: "Temporary rate limiting and increased latency in eu3. We're mitigating by routing traffic and applying temporary soft caps. We'll update in 30m." I'll draft and send once infra confirms the throttle payload.

infra-lead: On the infra side, we need to apply three immediate changes:
1) global conservative token rate-limit for region eu3: 0.8x of steady-state\n2) per-tenant softcaps for top-10 (60% of baseline)\n3) route non-SLA traffic via smart-router to eu-west1\nCommands I'm about to run (control-plane):
```
# apply global rate limit
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' https://control.redwood/api/v1/regions/eu3/rate_limits -d '{"global_factor":0.8, "ttl":1800}'

# apply per-tenant softcap
curl -X POST https://control.redwood/api/v1/tenants/bulk_quota -d '{"tenants":["redwood-marketing","beta-retail-1",...], "softcap_pct":60, "ttl":1800}'
```

sre-oncall: Please include a fallback remove step after 30m. Also pause bulk embeddings queue now (marcus will confirm once scaled).

marcus: embeddings-batch scaled to 0, confirmed. Pushing per-tenant softcaps now.

ops-bot: Action log: per-tenant softcaps queued by marcus at 1887654389. (reacted :white_check_mark: by sre-oncall)

deploy-bot: Applied region eu3 global rate-limit (0.8) at 1887654405. Telemetry will reflect change in ~45s.

sre-oncall: Observing early signal: image pull errors unchanged but overall ingress QPS to eu3 dropped ~22% after the routing change. p95 latency down to 145ms from 210ms. Good sign. Continuing to monitor for 15m.

irene: Please keep per-tenant metrics for the top 3 so we can see customer impact. We need to avoid cascading support tickets.

marcus: Logging per-tenant deltas to the incident channel dashboard. I'll surface any tenant that crosses >20% degradation.

product-ops: Draft sent to top-5 customers, waiting on infra confirmation text to include the exact TTL (30m). If timeline changes we'll update.

infra-lead: If we don't see improvement in 20m we should plan a controlled scale-out to eu3 from spare capacity in apse2, but that requires 45m to finish warmup. For now, keep softcaps + reroute.

sre-oncall: Agreed. Next update in 10m unless anything changes. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
